recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的漿細胞細胞質塞滿多個淡藍色、圓形、大小相近的球狀包涵體（Russell bodies），像一串葡萄，即 Mott 細胞；背景是大量具偏心核、藍色細胞質的漿細胞。
features: Plasma cell (arrow) with cytoplasm packed with multiple round, pale blue, uniform globules (Russell bodies) — Mott/grape cell
Nucleus of the Mott cell compressed to one side by the inclusions
Background of numerous plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, abundant deep blue cytoplasm and perinuclear hofs
Some background plasma cells are large with open chromatin and visible nucleoli (immature/atypical forms)
Occasional binucleate and irregular plasma cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a markedly increased population of plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, abundant basophilic cytoplasm and perinuclear clearing, including large forms with dispersed chromatin and nucleoli. One plasma cell (arrow) contains numerous round, pale blue cytoplasmic globules of accumulated immunoglobulin (Russell bodies), consistent with a Mott cell. Mott cells themselves are nonspecific, but the sheet-like background of atypical plasma cells is consistent with a plasma cell neoplasm; quantification and clonality studies are required.

ddx.vs: Reactive marrows contain Mott cells among a modest number of mature, polytypic plasma cells rather than sheets of atypical plasma cells.

ddx.dx: Vacuolated cells (e.g., Burkitt cells or blasts with vacuoles)
ddx.vs: Burkitt vacuoles are small, clear, lipid-containing punched-out holes in deeply basophilic cytoplasm, not uniform pale blue immunoglobulin globules.
Dutcher bodies are single intranuclear-appearing PAS-positive pseudoinclusions overlying the nucleus, favoring lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, rather than multiple cytoplasmic globules.
